Q: Airbyte Connector Builder test works, but creating a Source returns 401/403 on the same API endpoint A:

  1. Replace BearerAuthenticator with ApiKeyAuthenticator using explicit Bearer prefix — this eliminates any CDK version ambiguity in token injection

  2. Re-publish the connector from the Builder UI (don't manually build the image unless you know the CDK packaging setup)

  3. Verify the spec loads after publishing — go to the connector detail page and confirm the fields appear correctly before creating the Source

  4. Delete and recreate the Source after publishing the fix — existing Sources sometimes cache a broken config

Q: Lambda expression vs method reference A:

As user stuchl4n3k wrote in comments to the question, there may be exceptions occurring.

Let's consider that some variable field is null, then:

field = null;
runThisLater(()->field.method());
field = new SomeObject();

will not crash, while

field = null;
runThisLater(field::method);
field = new SomeObject();

will crash with java.lang.NullPointerException: Attempt to invoke virtual method 'java.lang.Class java.lang.Object.getClass()' at a method reference statement line, at least on Android.

Today's IntelliJ notes that the refactor "may change semantics" while suggesting this refactoring.

This happens when we do "referencing" of the instance method of a particular object. Why? Let’s check the first two paragraphs of 15.13.3. Run-Time Evaluation of Method References:

At run time, evaluation of a method reference expression is similar to evaluation of a class instance creation expression, insofar as normal completion produces a reference to an object. Evaluation of a method reference expression is distinct from invocation of the method itself.

First, if the method reference expression begins with an ExpressionName or a Primary, this subexpression is evaluated. If the subexpression evaluates to null, a NullPointerException is raised, and the method reference expression completes abruptly. If the subexpression completes abruptly, the method reference expression completes abruptly for the same reason.

In the case of a lambda expression, I'm unsure. The final type is derived at compile time from the method declaration. This is just simplification of what is going on exactly. But, let's assume that the method runThisLater has been declared as void runThisLater(SamType obj), where SamType is some functional interface. Then runThisLater(()->field.method()); translates into something like:

runThisLater(new SamType() {
    void doSomething() {
        field.method();
    }
});

Additional information:

  • 15.27.4. Run-Time Evaluation of Lambda Expressions
  • Translation of Lambda Expressions
  • State of the Lambda, version 3, where SAM was mentioned.
  • State of the Lambda, final.

Q: What is the best algorithm to compute the shortest path of a eulerian path in a directed graph? A:

Here is the pseudo code to find the eulerian path, if it exists:

ASSERT graph directed
ASSERT in-degree == out-degree for all vertices
SET vertex to first
WHILE true
    ADD vertex to circuit  
    FIND next vertex along unused edge
    MARK edge used
    IF no unused edge
        STOP

Q: How to turn off a bell in IntelliJ IDEA? A:

Although not related to IdeaVim plugin nor uncommenting lines, for IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1.4.1 (Ultimate Edition), there is a bell sound on the terminal. It can be disabled through Settings -> Tools -> Terminal and un-toggle the option Audible bell

Q: How can I deal with this javascript variables problem? A:

Let me walk you through the loop and the topTrait/topCount part in plain English, because once it clicks, you will find yourself using this pattern all the time.

Why do we need a loop at all?

After someone finishes the quiz, you end up with a little scoreboard - something like: open-minded got 3 votes, cautious got 1, empathetic got 1. The loop is just scanning through that scoreboard to find the biggest number. That's it. Nothing fancier than that.

Why topTrait and topCount?

Think of it like watching a race. As each runner crosses the finish line, you mentally note "okay, that's the fastest one so far." If the next runner beats them, you update your mental note. If not, you keep the old one.

topCount is the highest score recorded so far, and topTrait is the name of whichever personality type set it. We start both of them at zero and empty, because nobody has "won" yet.

Q: Is it Adapter or Strategy? I find it hard to differentiate it sometimes A:

Adapter design pattern allows incompatible objects to collaborate via additional common interface. By using this pattern you are trying to translate your code into “drawing” library. So, you want to make two things working together and have the ability to translate “console” to “file” and vice verse. I guess that’s not your case :)

In the meantime, by using Strategy pattern you trying to choose from two different “strategies”: whether you should draw into console or into file. And that’s why Strategy is a winner here.

But, following your next question about sending email, you can try to keep it simple and just apply SOLID Open Closed principle. You just need an interface IDrawer, which implementation will draw the shape as needed. The same with with the email sender. Just a single interface ISender, which implementation resolves email or any other sender.

Q: ABAP SALV ALV does not refresh after returning from ME52N when launched from Fiori tile A:

You need to hook into the Fiori back-navigation event instead of relying on post-navigate code. Use cl_lsapi_manager=>set_back_navigation_active to register a callback, so your refresh only triggers when the user navigates back from ME52N.

Here's the corrected approach:

" In your class definition, add the back-navigation interface
CLASS zcl_your_report_class DEFINITION
  ...
  INTERFACES if_lsapi_back_navigation.  " Add this
  ...

" In your hotspot handler, replace the navigate block with:
WHEN gc_fieldname-field1.
  ls_parameter-name  = gc_param_name-name2.
  ls_parameter-value = <lfs_final>-banfn.
  INSERT ls_parameter INTO TABLE lt_parameters_nav.
  CLEAR ls_parameter.

  " Register THIS object as the back-navigation handler BEFORE navigating
  CALL METHOD cl_lsapi_manager=>set_back_navigation_active
    EXPORTING
      back_navigation_handler = me   " 'me' must implement if_lsapi_back_navigation
    EXCEPTIONS
      error                   = 1
      not_supported           = 2
      OTHERS                  = 3.

  CALL METHOD cl_lsapi_manager=>navigate_to_transaction
    EXPORTING
      transaction       = gc_param_tcode-tcode1
      parameters_setget = lt_parameters_nav[]
    EXCEPTIONS
      error             = 1
      not_supported     = 2
      OTHERS            = 3.

  IF sy-subrc NE 0.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.
  " DO NOT call zrefresh_data here anymore


" Implement the back-navigation callback method:
METHOD if_lsapi_back_navigation~back_navigation_requested.
  " This fires when the user returns from ME52N in Fiori
  me->zrefresh_data( ).
ENDMETHOD.

Q: Apply Application.Match to string and elements in an array A:

Your base fault is - as Mate wrote - that arr isn't initialized in the first run

You can use this code - it uses the VBA Filter function to test wether a value is already part of an array or not.

Public Function getUniqueValuesFromRange(rg As Range) As Variant

Dim arrResult As Variant
ReDim arrResult(0 To rg.Cells.Count - 1)    'dim arrResult to the max

Dim iCell As Long, iResult As Long
Dim value As Variant

For iCell = 1 To rg.Cells.Count
    value = rg.Cells(iCell)
    If UBound(Filter(arrResult, value)) = -1 Then 'value is not part of arrResult
        arrResult(iResult) = value
        iResult = iResult + 1
    End If
Next

'it is "cheaper" to redim the array once at the end of the function
ReDim Preserve arrResult(iResult - 1)
getUniqueValuesFromRange = arrResult
End Function

You can call this function like this: arr = getUniqueValuesFromRange(Worksheets("table1").UsedRange.Columns("A"))

EDIT: you can use

If Not IsNumeric(Application.Match(value, arrResult, 0)) Then

instead of

If UBound(Filter(arrResult, value)) = -1 Then

If you have Excel 365 you can use the UNIQUE function as well

Public Function getUniqueValuesFromRange(rg As Range) As Variant 
With Application.WorksheetFunction
   getUniqueValuesFromRange= .Transpose(.Unique(rg))
End With
End Function

Be aware: there is no check, that you pass only one column ...
